_comment: Authorities this repo's CI CANNOT SEE, and the value last reconciled against
them. Read by tests/test_stated_cadences_faithful.py (which checks our prose
against it) and by tools/check_external_authorities.py (which runs in the
OTHER repo and checks it against the real file).
Every entry here is a CLAIM, not a fact. The fact is the `cron:`/`on:` line in
the file named below; this is a mirror of it, and a mirror nothing compares
back to its subject is #549's Shape 1 — the gate enforcing a proxy for the
promise. The far-side job is what stops that, so a record whose `repo` has no
reconciling job is worse than no record at all: it looks checked.
ONLY invisible authorities belong here. `.github/workflows/parity.yml` is in
this tree and resolves straight against its own file (see the test's
_IN_REPO) — mirroring it would manufacture a proxy where the promise was
Adding a record: add it here, then add the reconciling step in that repo, in
that order (the far side hard-fails on a record it cannot resolve, so the
reverse order is red for as long as it takes you to notice).
`aliases` is what the unannotated-claim tripwire keys on: the prose that
drifted in #311 never named a workflow file, so filename-matching alone would
have missed the two pages the whole gate exists for.

authorities.note: The 6-surface findings-agreement report (4 laterite surfaces + python-ags4 + the from-source DuckDB extension). Called 'weekly' on two published pages until #311; that was parity.yml's cadence, conflated with this.

The per-PR half of the same harness — the binding invariant over the four in-repo surfaces. Mirrored because our prose asserts its cadence too ('a per-PR gate plus a monthly full-matrix report'), and a sentence making two claims needs both resolvable or the completeness check cannot tell a dropped claim from an unmade one.
